request.subject: Both Engines Died Over New York City - part 2: The Passengers Who Waited on the Wings
request.title: Both Engines Died Over New York City (Part 2/3)
request.description:
The plane floated, water poured in, and passengers stood on the wings in the freezing wind until ferries arrived. Would you have stayed calm out there?

Part 2 of 3: Both Engines Died Over New York City

Sources:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Airways_Flight_1549
https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/AAR1003.pdf
https://flightsafety.org/asw-article/survival-on-the-hudson/

Stock footage: Pexels. Made with AI-assisted narration.

#shorts #truestory

extra_params.video_script: A jet full of people came gliding down onto a frigid river. In Part 1, geese knocked out both engines over New York City. The pilots set the plane down on the Hudson, and it floated. Cold water began pouring into the back of the cabin. Passengers climbed out onto the wings and waited in the freezing wind. Within minutes, ferry boats raced over and pulled people aboard. Every one of the 155 people on board survived. But investigators later tested whether the plane could have reached a runway instead. Subscribe so you don't miss Part 3.
